input.brief: Solo full-stack + AI engineer in Bandung, Indonesia; as the only developer at an industrial sealing factory he alone runs its entire live production estate: B2B RFQ platform, ERP admin, AI tax chatbot

direction.name: The pinned poster
direction.idea: Something stays put while everything else changes. A title holds its place across the viewport and the images beneath it swap; the name is split to two opposite corners and the page passes between the halves; a single frame stays centred while its contents change. Every scroll step is a new cover of the same magazine. The idea suits subjects that are a series (a book of portraits, a line-up, a collection, a set of projects): the fixed element says what the series is, the changing element shows its members.
direction.composition: A sticky layer holds the fixed element for the height of two to three viewports: usually the title at 10–14vw across the middle or top of the screen, or two words pinned to the top-left and bottom-right corners. Under it, a stack of full-height panels scrolls by, each a single large photograph (portrait 4:5, centred, 40–50% of the viewport wide) with one line of caption at the same small size everywhere. The title sits above the images in the stacking order and uses `mix-blend-mode: difference` or a solid colour that reads on every panel. When the pinned run ends, the page releases into ordinary flowing sections with a narrow measure. Build with `position: sticky`; never hijack the scroll.
direction.typography: The pinned title is the only large type on the page. Captions and body share one small size (15–17px). Tight tracking and solid weight so the title reads over photographs.
direction.colour: One strong title colour against a pale or dark ground. Each panel may take its own flat ground colour sampled from its photograph.
direction.imagery: A series of photographs with the same crop ratio and the same framing (all portraits, all objects, all rooms), so that swapping them reads as one image changing. Five to eight in the pinned run.
direction.richness: Repetition with change. The fixed title makes each new photograph feel like an event, so the photographs must be good and consistent.
direction.pitfalls: If the title is not legible over every panel, the idea fails: test each one. Keep the pinned run under six viewports or it feels like a trap. On a phone the title shrinks to 16–18vw and stays pinned at the top; panels become full-width. A pin longer than three screens, or one where the screens under it are nearly empty, read in blind tests as a stuck page. Every screen under the pin needs its own content, and nothing may pass over the pinned words.

hero.name: Name split to corners
hero.blueprint: The name is cut into two halves that stay pinned to opposite corners while the page passes between them. A layer with `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` and `pointer-events: none` holds both: the first word top-left, 28px from the top and left edges; the second word bottom-right, 28px from the bottom and right edges. Both are set at clamp(72px, 9vw, 140px), line-height 0.85, in white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` so they read on every panel beneath. On the first screen the stage between them is a paper-white panel on columns 1–9 and one full-height photograph on columns 10–12 touching the top, right and bottom edges. The supporting sentence, 20px and max 34ch, starts at column 3 at 44% of the height; the single action is a text link with an arrow directly under it. Three text links are stacked at 15px along the right edge of the white panel at mid-height. The rest of the panel is empty. Later panels, full-height photographs and text panels of different widths, scroll under the pinned halves for three to five viewports; then the layer releases into ordinary sections.
hero.mobile: Both halves stay pinned: the first word top-left and the second bottom-right, each at 15vw with 16px margins. Between them every panel is a full-width photograph 56svh tall followed by its sentence at 17px. On the first screen the photograph crosses the middle band with the supporting sentence and the action link beneath it. The stacked links collapse to one word at the top-right corner.
hero.headline: The name in two halves (two words, or one word cut at a syllable), each up to about 9 characters at 9vw, one per corner, with no other headline.

type.note: A flat-sided extended grotesk in heavy capitals, wide enough that two words fill the screen, with a neutral sans kept small. Suits portfolios, real estate, travel and brand sites that want a broad, confident wordmark.

palette.name: Teal on paper
palette.note: Cool white paper and a single teal used for every word, shape and button, with no black anywhere. The accent is that same teal filled solid, for the button and for one inverted band with paper-coloured type.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Pinned title, portraits pass
sections.blueprint: A wrapper tall enough for its portraits: about 90svh per person, up to six people. A `position: sticky; top: 0` layer of 100svh holds the heading, two words at clamp(88px, 12vw, 180px), leading 0.85, centred at mid-height, in white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` so it reads over ground and photographs alike. Beneath it in the stacking order, portraits scroll past in normal flow: each a 4:5 photograph 26–30vw wide, alternately starting at column 2 and ending at column 11, 60svh apart, so each one passes behind a different half of the heading. Under each portrait's left corner: the name at 18px, the role at 14px in the soft ink, and one sentence of up to 30 words in a 280px measure. The last portrait is followed by 40svh of empty ground before the heading releases. Square corners. Nothing else is on screen.
sections.mobile: The heading shrinks to 17vw and pins 16px from the top instead of at mid-height. Portraits become 72% wide, alternating between the left and right margins, 48px apart, each with name, role and sentence beneath at the portrait's width.

sections.name: Full panels, one midline row
sections.blueprint: Four to seven consecutive panels, each 100vw by 100svh, butted together with no gap. Each panel is one photograph of the project cropped much tighter than its frame (`object-fit: cover` with the image scaled to 130%), so a detail fills the screen. The same three-part text row sits at exactly 50% of the height on every panel, in white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` or over a neutral dark scrim band 90px tall: the date or year at the left margin at 15px, the project title in capitals at clamp(22px, 2vw, 30px) starting 10% in from the left, and one fact (location, client, number of pieces) at the right margin at 15px. Because the row never moves, scrolling reads like turning plates in a book. Panels may be `position: sticky; top: 0` so each slides over the last. There is no section heading; the first panel's title row is the heading.
sections.mobile: Panels are 100vw by 82svh. The row drops to the bottom of each panel, 20px above its edge: the title at 22px on the first line, then date at the left and fact at the right on a second line at 13px, over the same scrim band.

sections.name: Names running off the edges
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed band in a flat colour, about 34vh tall, holding a single line of names that is cropped by both viewport edges. The names are set at 8vw in the display weight, `white-space: nowrap`, separated by a solid round dot one third of the cap height, and the line moves slowly to the left (a CSS `translateX` animation over 40 seconds on a duplicated track, paused under `prefers-reduced-motion`). The band has no heading. Its meaning comes from one sentence at 18px set directly below the band at the left margin on the page ground, stating plainly who these names are. Supplied logos may replace names if all are available as single-colour SVGs at 0.8em height; do not mix logos and set names in one line. The band butts against the sections above and below with no gap.
sections.mobile: The band is 22vh tall with names at 15vw, still cropped at both edges and still moving. The explaining sentence sits under it at 16px with 20px margins. Do not add a second line running the opposite way; one line is the idea.

sections.name: Figure on the photograph's edge
sections.blueprint: One full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 88svh, and one figure set on it the way a film title sits on a frame. The figure, with its unit, is at clamp(120px, 17vw, 280px), leading 0.8, in paper colour, hugging the bottom-left corner with 24px margins, its baseline nearly on the photograph's lower edge. A neutral dark scrim covers only the bottom 35% of the image for legibility. On the same baseline at the right margin, right-aligned, a sentence of up to 26ch at 18px explains the figure. At the top-left, small at 20–24px, sits the heading of two to four words; the middle of the photograph stays clear. Two smaller supporting figures may follow below the photograph, on the ground: each at 40px with a one-line caption beside it, starting at columns 1 and 7, 40px under the image. Choose a figure that belongs to the picture: a height, a distance, a temperature, a year.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 80svh, cropped to its subject. The figure sits bottom-left at 30vw; the sentence moves above it at 16px, left-aligned. Supporting figures stack under the photograph at 32px, each with its caption on the line beneath.

sections.name: The email as display type
sections.blueprint: The section is 100svh in the inverse of the page's colours. A single email address is set as one line of display type spanning the content width: the font-size is fitted so the address runs from margin to margin (about 7–9vw for 20 characters; break after the @ onto two lines if it is longer than 26), light or regular weight, tight tracking, sitting on a baseline 12vh above the bottom edge. It is a `mailto:` link; on hover the whole line takes the accent ink. In the top-left corner, a sentence of up to 12 words at 20–22px says what to write about. In the two bottom corners at 14px: phone and city at the left, two or three social links at the right. No heading and no form. For a pinned ending, make the section `position: sticky; bottom: 0` beneath the page so the previous section lifts off it.
sections.mobile: The address breaks after the @ onto two lines at 11.5vw, left-aligned, sitting at 55% of an 86svh screen. The sentence sits at the top-left at 18px. Phone, city and social links stack at the bottom-left at 15px with 12px between them.

sections.name: Photograph half, menu half
sections.blueprint: A split footer one viewport tall. The left half is a single photograph filling columns 1–6 edge to edge, cropped hard by the left and bottom viewport edges: a close crop of the page's main subject, larger than it appeared anywhere above. The right half, on a flat field, is the site's menu set large: five or six section names stacked as links at about 2.6vw bold, 28px apart, starting at column 8 and 80px from the top. Rows are separated by space only; on hover a row's label shifts right by 12px and the others drop to the softer ink. Under the menu, 64px lower, two short blocks at 15px side by side: contact and social. The legal line runs along the very bottom of the right half at 12px. The wordmark sits small at the top of the right half, on the menu's left edge.
sections.mobile: The photograph leads at full width and 50svh, cropped tight. The menu follows on the flat field at 8vw per item with 20px between items, then contact and social stacked at 15px, then the legal line at 12px. The wordmark sits small above the menu.

references.name: Glitch&Grit
references.idea: Every screen is one project: two half-width footage columns with the project name stacked dead centre across their seam in a single flat pastel that changes per project.
references.hero: Black viewport split down its vertical centre. The left half holds a huge flat grey flower silhouette bleeding off the left and bottom edges; the right half is black with a few tiny video thumbnails drifting through. Dead centre, straddling the split, sits a two-line uppercase title in mint green, about 11vw per line, lines almost touching, spanning roughly 70% of the width. Two tiny category lines sit directly above it and a tiny 'view full project' link directly below, all in the same green. Navigation is six small bold white words pinned to the frame: three links across the top edge, the three-part studio name across the bottom edge.
references.type: Elza only, weight 900, uppercase, tracking -0.05em so letters nearly collide, line-height under 1. Just two sizes exist: roughly 158px project titles and 12px bold caps for nav, tags and links, a 13:1 jump with nothing in between.
references.colour: #000000 #999999 #9ae187 #93f1f7 #dcc8ff #fbb060 — Black ground and dark-graded footage. The only flat colour is the title lock-up, which takes a new candy pastel per project: mint, cyan, lilac, cornflower, lemon, orange.
references.imagery: Client film footage in two half-width columns per screen, cropped tight, graded dark, square edges, the two columns vertically offset against each other. One flat grey cut-out flower shape opens the sequence.
references.layout: No margins or containers. Each project is a full viewport cut into two equal media columns with one centred title lock-up. Fixed corner navigation frames every screen; fourteen screens repeat the same slide with different footage and title colour.

sections.description: Each scroll stop is a project slide. Two half-width media columns fill the viewport edge to edge and travel vertically at different offsets, so their top and bottom seams never align. Centred over the join: a two-line 11vw uppercase title in one flat pastel, with two or three 12px tag lines stacked above and a 12px 'view full project' or 'coming soon' line beneath. Title colour changes on every slide; nothing else does.

There is no footer block. The last screen is simply another project slide, and the studio name fixed along the bottom edge in three pieces (first word bottom-left, ampersand bottom-centre, last word bottom-right) does the footer's job on every screen, mirroring the three nav words fixed along the top edge at the same size and weight.

steal: Break the studio name into three words pinned bottom-left, bottom-centre and bottom-right, mirroring three nav links across the top, so the viewport frame itself is the logo.
Give each project slide one flat pastel used only for its title and tags, so a colour change is the sole signal that the project changed.
Split the viewport into two media columns that scroll at different offsets and set the title across the seam so the type stitches the halves together.
references.media: Media fills the whole first screen: a flat grey cut-out flower on the left half and a scatter of small thumbnails on the right that grows into a collage round the title. Then video is the main medium: each project is two full 720x900 half panes of muted, looping footage moving in opposite directions, with the title straddling the seam; about 24 pieces of footage or illustration across twelve projects.
references.motion: After a 10.7s load the thumbnail grid fills the right half by 1.2s and scales into a cluster by 4.5s, and Lenis then runs 40 scrubbed ScrollTriggers on empty 855px track divs: per project the left pane and half-title travel one way and the right ones the other (titles ±270px, panes ±180px), lining up only at the centre, and the scroll resets for an endless loop. Panes grow from an edge by scaleY over 0.5s, tags slide on y over 0.5s power2, and there is no reduced-motion rule.

references.name: Revelatio Studio
references.idea: The team photograph is the hero: it starts as a small CRT-curved mosaic of typographic glyphs and resolves into a full-bleed group portrait as you scroll.
references.hero: Pure black viewport. Centred, about 58% of the width and 57% of the height, is a canvas showing a group photo rebuilt from tiny coloured glyphs, its edges barrel-distorted like a CRT tube; it is dim, so black dominates. The headline is modest: two lines at 2.5vw in regular-weight grotesk, flush to the bottom-left corner with a 30px margin. Navigation is split into two small dark-grey rounded rectangles: logo mark plus four links top-left, language switch and contact top-right. Nothing else; roughly 80% of the screen is black.
references.type: Neue Haas Grotesk Text 55 Roman is the only face and weight. Headline just 36px with -0.03em tracking against 15px body; hierarchy comes from position and grey value. The footer city list jumps to roughly 5vw; the digest records a 12.5vw maximum.
references.colour: #000000 #ffffff #2b2b2b #8a8a8a — Black intro and footer, white work and capabilities sections. The interface has no accent; all colour comes from project thumbnails and the faint tints inside the glyph mosaic.
references.imagery: A studio group portrait rendered as a glyph mosaic on canvas, then as a dim near-full-bleed photograph; project tiles are square-cornered brand visuals in saturated flat colours, set on white with caption rows beneath.
references.layout: About 30px side margins throughout. Black full-screen opening, then a white work grid mixing one large tile with a narrow companion and a three-up row, a three-column plain-text capabilities list, and a black footer of oversized dim text. Captions sit under images, tags right-aligned.

sections.description: Pinned for about two viewports: the hero canvas grows with scroll from a centred 58%-wide mosaic to a near full-bleed image with a thin black margin, while the glyph cells shrink until the picture reads as a dim photograph of about twenty people. The headline scrolls away and only the two nav boxes remain in the top corners.

White background. First row: one large landscape tile spanning roughly two-thirds of the width beside a narrower tile about one-third wide and half as tall, top-aligned. Second row: three equal tiles. All square-cornered with about 16px gutters. Beneath each: project name at left, two tiny grey tags right-aligned on the same line, then a two-line grey description at about 11px. A small underlined see-all link with an arrow sits below the grid at left.

White section opened by a hairline and a tiny label. Three text columns, each with a small grey category title and beneath it a tight stack of eight to ten service names in 15px regular grotesk at about 1.2 line-height, with no bullets, icons or cards. Columns share the work grid's left edges, leaving the right third partly empty.

Black full-viewport block filled with a run-on, comma-separated list of client cities set at about 5vw in very dark grey, barely visible against black, wrapping over seven flush-left lines. Exactly one city, the last, is lit white, which implies a cycling highlight. The nav boxes stay fixed at the top corners.

steal: Render a photograph as a grid of small coloured glyphs on canvas and let scroll increase its size and resolution until it becomes the real photo.
Hold the hero headline at 2.5vw in a bottom corner and let a dim central image and empty black carry the scale.
Set a long list in near-invisible dark grey at display size and light one item at a time.
references.media: A centred 16:10 canvas covering 60% of the width and height plays the team film as a dot matrix with a curved, tube-like outline, and grows to cover the whole screen over three screens of scroll. Below: an asymmetric two-plus-one then three-up grid of 16:9 work cards (video players scaled to 133% of the card so the letterboxing is cropped), a cursor image trail over a pinned city list, a draggable marquee of result cards, and a slider of cards with staggered image heights bleeding off the right edge; square corners.
references.motion: No preloader was seen and the hero is composed at 400ms (load 23s); Lenis then holds two sticky 900px stages, the hero screen scaling from 60% to full bleed over 2700px and one city at a time lighting up over 3600px. The ground flips black, white, black by section with a 0.35s ease on colour across about 11,000 nodes, stat numerals roll like an odometer, and transforms run 0.4s on cubic-bezier(0.625,0.05,0,1) with 0.8s exits on (0.625,0,0.875,0).

references.name: Belen Jones
references.idea: The whole portfolio is one screen: a slowly turning 3D box skinned with project footage behind a floor-to-ceiling list of outlined client names.
references.hero: One viewport, no scroll. A flat pastel field (periwinkle on load) with a large black-edged 3D box, about half the viewport wide, rotating right of centre; each face shows a project film still. Over everything, nine project names are stacked flush-left from top edge to bottom edge in an ultra-bold extended sans at 7.6vw, caps, drawn as thin outlines only, lines almost touching; the active name is filled solid. Two small white pill buttons sit top-right; a two-line mono location and clock bottom-right. On first load only the box is visible, drifting in from the right with its texture mirrored, before the list appears.
references.type: Monument Extended Ultrabold caps at 109px with line-height near 0.95, drawn as a 1px outline and filled only for the active item. Roboto Mono in tiny caps for buttons, location and time. Two sizes in total, about 10:1.
references.colour: #c3cbe5 #141414 #efd3da #e6dccd #cfd3cb #f9d2bf — A flat pastel background that swaps per project (periwinkle, pink, sand, sage, peach) against the black box and dark outline type. The footage supplies the saturated colour.
references.imagery: Campaign and music-video stills mapped as textures onto the faces of a rotating WebGL cuboid with black edges; images skew in perspective and blur while turning. No flat images anywhere.
references.layout: A single fixed screen. The type column sits flush to the left edge with about 10px margin and fills the full height; the 3D object occupies centre-right behind the type. Utility items are pinned to the right-hand corners.

sections.description: The list is the navigation. Hovering a name fills that line solid (dark, or with a clipped piece of footage showing through the letters), swaps the page background to that project's pastel, and turns the box to a face carrying the matching film still, enlarged to roughly 45% of the viewport. All other names stay as hairline outlines drawn over the box.

Mobile variant: the list is dropped. A hairline-bordered bar across the top is divided into four cells with mono caps labels for back, name, contact and next. Below it a single portrait video frame about 57% of the width is centred on the pastel field with large empty space above and below; projects advance one at a time.

steal: Set a project list as outline-only giant caps over the media and fill just the active line, so the list is both navigation and texture.
Map project stills onto the faces of one rotating box so changing project is a turn of the object, not a page change.
Assign each project its own flat pastel background and cross-fade the whole field on hover.
